content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL: Rewrite using synthesis language: a) 'Books say dolphins are smart. Scientists also say this.' → 'Multiple sources agree that...' b) 'Source 1 says climate change is human-caused. Source 2 disagrees.' → 'While... argues..., however... suggests...'

2. VOCABULARY: Match: [1] synthesize [2] contradict [3] confirm [4] finding → [a] say something is wrong [b] combine info from many sources [c] verify that something is true [d] a result discovered by research

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  When you have gathered notes from multiple sources, the next skill is SYNTHESIS — combining information from different sources to create new understanding.
content: 📖 When you have gathered notes from multiple sources, the next skill is SYNTHESIS — combining information from different sources to create new understanding.

Beginning researchers often simply list facts: 'Source A says X. Source B says Y. Source C says Z.' This is a summary, not synthesis. True synthesis connects ideas and finds relationships between them.

Good synthesis says: 'Multiple sources agree that X, although Source C provides a different perspective by saying Z.' Or: 'The evidence shows a clear pattern: as X increases, Y also increases, which is supported by three separate studies.'
When synthesizing, look for: AGREEMENTS (what do most sources agree on?), DISAGREEMENTS (where do sources differ?), and GAPS (what questions are still unanswered?).
The ability to synthesize information is one of the most valuable academic skills. It shows you are not just collecting facts, but truly understanding your topic.
